key_insight: Differentiating through a cylinder-wake simulation enables closed-loop policies to achieve approximately 8% drag reduction and 99.6% suppression of lift fluctuations in eight policy updates.
engineering_relevance: Gradient-based feedback control offers a potentially interaction-efficient route to suppressing vortex shedding with local velocity sensing and synthetic-jet actuation.
method: Map local velocity measurements to synthetic-jet amplitude.
Backpropagate control-loss gradients through simulated flow and differentiable jet boundary conditions.
Update policy parameters using reverse-mode automatic differentiation.
evidence_signal: In a 2D confined wake at Re=100, training used about 78 shedding periods of forward simulation; tests showed consistent responses across three activation phases and recovery after upstream disturbances.
watch_item: Results are limited to a 2D confined flow at Re=100; transfer to turbulent 3D flows or physical hardware remains unestablished.
paper_title: Closed-loop policy optimisation for cylinder wake control via differentiable simulation
